q: What is Rule 1 of the rules of firearms safety?

wrong: Keep the weapon on safe at all times
Always clear the weapon before handing it off
Know your target and what is beyond it
file: TC 3-22.9 - Rifle and Carbine (C3).pdf
quote: Rule 1: Treat Every Weapon as if it is Loaded
why: TC 3-22.9 lists treating every weapon as loaded as the first rule of firearms safety.

q: What four colors are used for weapon safety status?
answer: Green, amber, red, and black
file: TC 3-22.9 - Rifle and Carbine (C3).pdf
quote: It is a standard code that uses common colors (green, amber, red, and black) to represent the level of readiness for a given weapon.
why: Weapon safety status uses four colors from fully safe (green) to not safe (black).

q: What is the condition of an M4 in weapon safety status red?
answer: On SAFE, magazine locked in the well, round in the chamber, bolt forward
wrong: On SEMI, no magazine, chamber empty, bolt forward
On SAFE, no magazine, chamber empty, bolt locked to the rear
On SAFE, magazine inserted, chamber empty, bolt forward

q: What does the weapons control status WEAPONS TIGHT mean?

wrong: Engage only if engaged or ordered to engage
Engage targets not positively identified as friendly
Do not engage under any circumstances

why: Weapons tight sits between hold (only if engaged or ordered) and free (anything not identified as friendly).

wrong: Chambering, feeding, firing, locking, extracting, unlocking, cocking, ejecting

quote: The phases of the cycle of function in order are— Feeding. Chambering. Locking. Firing. Unlocking. Extracting. Ejecting. Cocking.
why: TC 3-22.9 lists the eight phases in this exact order.

q: What type of operating system do the M4 and M16 use?
answer: A direct impingement gas operating system
file: TC 3-22.9 - Rifle and Carbine (C3).pdf
quote: The M4- and M16-series weapons use a direct impingement gas operating system.

q: Who is authorized to approach dud ordnance on a Camp Ripley grenade range?
answer: Only EOD
file: CRTC Reg 210-2 - Camp Ripley Range Regulation (Jan 2026).pdf
quote: Only EOD is authorized to approach DUD ordnance.
why: Duds must also be reported to range control.

q: May a Soldier pick up UXO and remove it from the training area?
answer: No, unauthorized personnel are prohibited from handling or removing UXO
wrong: Yes, if they turn it in to the ASP
Yes, if it is a practice round
file: CRTC Reg 210-2 - Camp Ripley Range Regulation (Jan 2026).pdf
quote: Unauthorized personnel are prohibited from handling UXO or removing them from the FTA.
why: UXO is reported, not touched.

q: What is the minimum PPE level 0 on a Camp Ripley range?
answer: Army Combat Uniform with hearing and eye protection
wrong: Body armor with plates and helmet
file: CRTC Reg 210-2 - Camp Ripley Range Regulation (Jan 2026).pdf
quote: 0 (Min Req) Army Combat Uniform/Standard Utility Uniform, hearing/eye protection
why: The commander determines the PPE level; level 0 is the minimum.

q: What is the downrange speed limit at Camp Ripley unless otherwise posted?
answer: 25 MPH, and 15 MPH on one-lane roads
wrong: 35 MPH, and 25 MPH on one-lane roads
file: CRTC Reg 210-2 - Camp Ripley Range Regulation (Jan 2026).pdf
quote: The speed limit is 25 MPH unless otherwise posted. On one lane roads the speed limit is 15 MPH.
why: Speeding costs the unit points under the safety policy.

q: What happens immediately when a range barrier is breached?
answer: Immediate cease-fire of affected training areas, ranges, and firing points
wrong: Firing continues while range control investigates
Only the nearest firing point stops
The unit files a report at the end of the day
file: CRTC Reg 210-2 - Camp Ripley Range Regulation (Jan 2026).pdf
quote: Barrier Breach requires the following actions: Immediate Cease-Fire of affected Training Areas, Ranges, and Firing Points.
why: Fire stays stopped until the surface danger zone is confirmed clear.

q: Recite the Warrior Ethos.
answer: I will always place the mission first. I will never accept defeat. I will never quit. I will never leave a fallen comrade.
wrong: I will always place my Soldiers first. I will never surrender. I will never quit. I will never fail.
I am an American Soldier. I am a Warrior. I serve the people. I live the Army Values.
Loyalty, duty, respect, selfless service, honor, integrity, personal courage.
file: TC 3-21.75 - The Warrior Ethos and Soldier Combat Skills (Aug 2013).pdf
quote: I will always place the mission first. I will never accept defeat. I will never quit. I will never leave a fallen comrade.
why: The Warrior Ethos is the four lines embedded in the Soldier's Creed.

q: What are the three individual movement techniques?
answer: Low crawl, high crawl, and rush
wrong: Traveling, traveling overwatch, and bounding overwatch
Low crawl, side step, and roll
file: TC 3-21.75 - The Warrior Ethos and Soldier Combat Skills (Aug 2013).pdf
quote: you may move in one of three other methods known as individual movement techniques (IMT) — low crawl, high crawl, or rush.
why: Traveling and bounding overwatch are unit movement techniques, not IMT.

q: How long should each individual rush last?
answer: 3 to 5 seconds
file: TC 3-21.75 - The Warrior Ethos and Soldier Combat Skills (Aug 2013).pdf
quote: The rush is the fastest way to move from one position to another (Figure 7-2). Each rush should last from 3 to 5 seconds.
why: Short rushes keep enemy gunners from tracking you.

q: What is the difference between cover and concealment?
answer: Cover protects you from fire and observation; concealment only hides you from observation
wrong: Cover hides you; concealment protects you from bullets
Concealment is man-made; cover is always natural
file: TC 3-21.75 - The Warrior Ethos and Soldier Combat Skills (Aug 2013).pdf
quote: Cover, made of natural or man-made materials, gives protection from bullets, fragments of exploding rounds, flame, nuclear effects, biological and chemical agents, and enemy observation
why: Concealment does not protect you from enemy fire.

q: What does SALUTE stand for?
answer: Size, activity, location, uniform, time, equipment
wrong: Size, area, location, unit, terrain, enemy
Situation, activity, location, unit, time, enemy
Size, activity, location, unit, terrain, equipment
file: TC 3-21.75 - The Warrior Ethos and Soldier Combat Skills (Aug 2013).pdf
quote: The size, activity, location, uniform, time, equipment (SALUTE) format is an example of Level I reporting.
why: SALUTE is the standard format for reporting enemy information.

q: What procedure do you follow when handling EPWs and detainees?
answer: The 5 Ss and T: search, segregate, silence, speed, safeguard, and tag
wrong: Segregate, silence, sit, stand, search, tag
file: TC 3-21.75 - The Warrior Ethos and Soldier Combat Skills (Aug 2013).pdf
quote: In handling EPWs/detainees, follow the procedure of search, segregate, silence, speed, safeguard, and tag (the 5 Ss and T).
why: EPWs must be treated humanely under the law of war.

q: What is the standard for performing a function check on an M4?
answer: Verify it is clear and check it works in each selector position, with all steps in sequence
wrong: Fire one round on each selector position
Disassemble and inspect the bolt carrier group
file: STP 21-1-SMCT - Soldier's Manual of Common Tasks, Warrior Skills Level 1 (Govt Only).pdf
quote: Verify the M16/M4 is clear and conduct a function check to ensure that the weapon operates properly with the selector switch in each position.
why: Task 071-COM-0029 also requires all steps to be performed in sequence.

q: In task Adjust Indirect Fire, how accurately must you locate the target and how fast must you send the initial call for fire?
answer: Within 250 meters, initial call for fire within 3 minutes
file: STP 21-24-SMCT - Soldier's Manual of Common Tasks, Warrior Leader Skills Levels 2-4 (Sep 2008).pdf
quote: Determine the target location to within 250 meters of its actual location. Transmit the initial call for fire within 3 minutes after identifying the target.
why: Adjustments must then be sent within 45 seconds after each spotting.
